data.name: Sanja
data.gender_notes: Sanja is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Slavic word ‘sanjati’ which means ‘healer’ or ‘helper’. In Christian tradition, this name is associated with St. John the Baptist, who was known as the ‘voice of one crying in the wilderness’ and a precursor to Jesus. Sanja embodies the traits of compassion, strength, and selflessness. The name Sanja carries the meaning “Healer, Helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Sanja usually hope their child will grow to embody healer, helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing divine intervention and guidance in times of need.
data.etymology: Sanja belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Healer, Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sanja total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sanja holds cultural significance within primarily Eastern European communities, particularly in Serbia and Croatia. In Croatia, for instance, Sanja is the feminine form of the name Sanko, which is popular among the Roma (Gypsy) population. Sanja is also a common name among the Serbian Orthodox population.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Sanja evokes the image of St. John the Baptist, a prophet of great importance in Christianity. Known for his key role in preparing the way for Jesus, St. John the Baptist served as a symbolic healer and helper in spiritual terms. Sanja as a name inspires us to embody the virtues of faith, resilience, determination, and selflessness to help others and uplift the spiritual realm.
